Calculating Reaction Distances

Name: ______________

Date: _______

Use a mathematical model (distance = speed * time) to generate data to tell us about how speed affects reaction distance. Use the table below to record your data. In the second column, the speed in miles per hour (MPH) has already been converted to meters per second (m/s) for you to make the calculations more straightforward.

Assume that the average reaction time of a non-distracted adult in the U.S. is .75 seconds. Assume that distracted doubles reaction time.

Speed in MPH Speed in m/s Stopping distance if driver is not distracted (in meters) Stopping distance if driver is distracted (in meters)
7 3    
20 9    
55 25    
67 30    
80 36    
100 45    

When you have finished filling in the table, read through your solutions.

  • Is it clear how you got to this solution? If not, take a moment to make your work more visible.
  • Is it clear what the solution is? If not, take a moment to circle or underline your solutions.
  • Does each solution make sense as a possible outcome in the real world? Take a moment to read through and flag data that doesn’t make sense. Re-do the calculation to make sure it is not an error.
